comparisons.peer_topic: Deferred tax assets and valuation allowance assessment
comparisons.peer_summary: Management concluded no valuation allowance is needed for U.K. and U.S. federal/state NOL carryforwards due to sufficient future taxable income, though a material change in estimates could reassess this. Approximately $5.0 billion of permanent investments in non-U.S. subsidiaries had not provided for U.S. federal income taxes, which would result in a $1.0 billion deferred tax liability if recorded.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Bank of America disclose specific management conclusions regarding the realizability of NOL carryforward deferred tax assets without valuation allowances. JPMorgan lists specific carryforward amounts (e.g., $496 million U.S. federal NOLs, $958 million non-U.S. NOLs) and their expiration windows (2026-2041 or unlimited). Bank of America similarly concludes that no valuation allowance is necessary for U.K. and U.S. federal/state NOL carryforwards because estimated future taxable income will be sufficient, but also discloses a hypothetical $1.0 billion deferred tax liability for permanently reinvested non-U.S. subsidiary investments where taxes have not been provided.

sentences.text: State and local capital loss carryforwards were $914 million, U.S. federal NOL carryforwards were $496 million, non-U.S. NOL carryforwards were $958 million, and other U.S. federal tax attributes were $111 million.
If not utilized, a portion of the U.S. federal NOL carryforwards and other U.S. federal tax attributes will expire between 2026 and 2036 whereas others have an unlimited carryforward period.

Management concluded that no valuation allowance was necessary to reduce the deferred tax assets related to the U.K. NOL carryforwards and U.S. federal and certain state NOL carryforwards since estimated future taxable income will be sufficient to utilize these assets prior to their expiration.
If the Corporation were to record the associated deferred tax liability, the amount would be approximately $1.0 billion.

comparisons.peer_summary: The majority of Citi's U.S. federal and all New York State and City net operating loss carry-forwards have a 20-year carry-forward period, which Citi believes is sufficient to fully utilize these DTAs due to forecasts of sufficient U.S. taxable income and New York's taxation of non-U.S. income.
comparisons.comparison: Both companies disclose the carryforward periods for their net operating loss (NOL) carryforwards. JPMorgan specifies that portions of U.S. federal and non-U.S. NOLs expire between 2026 and 2036/2041, with some having unlimited carryforward periods. Citi explicitly states that its U.S. federal and New York State/City NOL carry-forwards are subject to a 20-year carry-forward period, which it believes is sufficient to fully utilize the assets due to forecasts of sufficient taxable income.

sentences.text: If not utilized, a portion of the U.S. federal NOL carryforwards and other U.S. federal tax attributes will expire between 2026 and 2036 whereas others have an unlimited carryforward period.
Similarly, certain non-U.S. NOL carryforwards will expire between 2026 and 2041 whereas others have an unlimited carryforward period.
The majority of Citi's U.S. federal net operating loss carry-forward and all of its New York State and City net operating loss carry-forwards are subject to a carry-forward period of 20 years.
This provides enough time to fully utilize the DTAs pertaining to these existing NOL carry-forwards.

comparisons.peer_topic: Net Operating Loss Carryforwards and Expiration
comparisons.peer_summary: The firm recorded deferred tax assets of $786 million (2024) and $929 million (2023) related to net operating loss carryforwards, with a valuation allowance of $328 million (2024) and $396 million (2023); these carryforwards begin to expire in 2025, which would not have a material impact.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclose deferred tax assets associated with net operating loss (NOL) carryforwards and discuss the risk of expiration. JPMorgan reports $352 million in deferred tax assets for carryforwards with specific expiration dates ranging from 2026 to 2041. Goldman Sachs reports $786 million in deferred tax assets for NOL carryforwards, noting that if not utilized, these carryforwards begin to expire in 2025, though the firm assesses this expiration would not have a material impact on operations.
